answer: A timber ring is read, not painted. Each identity's attestation signal is a hash of its own history, so a clone's signal is only as deep as the uptime it has. The network measures pairwise signal similarity: a cluster whose signals correlate past a threshold is a plantation, and its weight is discounted sublinearly up to a zenith cap. To make K identities each count fully, a farm must desynchronize them and give every clone a distinct, earned history — the months of uptime it was skipping. One tree's rings verify; a forest of identical trees is a plantation.
